questionText: What does the acronym HTML stand for?
explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language, the standard markup language for creating web documents.

questionText: Which HTML tag is used to define the largest heading?
explanation: <h1> defines the most important and largest heading, whereas <h6> defines the smallest heading.

questionText: Which HTML tag creates a clickable hyperlink to another web page?
explanation: The <a> (anchor) tag combined with the href attribute creates a clickable hyperlink.

questionText: Which attribute is required on an `` tag to provide alternative text for screen readers?
explanation: The 'alt' attribute provides accessible alternative text if the image fails to load and for assistive screen readers.

questionText: Which tag creates an unordered (bulleted) list in HTML?
explanation: <ul> defines an unordered (bulleted) list, while <ol> defines an ordered (numbered) list. List items use <li>.

questionText: Which HTML tag is used to create a single-line text input field inside a form?
explanation: <input type="text"> creates a single-line text input field, whereas <textarea> creates a multi-line input.

questionText: What is the key difference between `<div>` and `<span>` in default HTML rendering?

options.text: There is no difference in default styling

explanation: By default, <div> is a block-level container that starts on a new line and spans full width; <span> is an inline container.

questionText: Which HTML5 semantic element is intended to hold self-contained content, such as a blog post or news story?
explanation: The <article> element specifies independent, self-contained content that could be distributed or reused on its own.

questionText: How do you open a hyperlink in a new browser tab in HTML?
explanation: Setting target="_blank" instructs the browser to open the linked document in a new tab or window.

questionText: What does the `<!DOCTYPE html>` declaration at the very top of an HTML document do?

options.text: It links an external CSS stylesheet
It tells the web browser to render the page in standard modern HTML5 mode rather than quirks mode
It encrypts the HTML page with HTTPS
It is an HTML tag that creates the document title

explanation: <!DOCTYPE html> is an instruction that informs the browser of the document type, ensuring standard-compliant HTML5 rendering without quirks mode.
